title: Which frames with four right angles are rectangles, which squares?
description: Four shapes each have all four angles equal to ninety degrees, with different side lengths. The video checks each against the rectangle rule and the square rule, then Keeko doubts that the four by four shape can be a rectangle.
teaching_notes: One idea: a rectangle needs four right angles, and a square is a rectangle whose sides are also all equal. Watch for students who push the square out of the rectangles because it has a name of its own.

source: Four quadrilaterals each have all angles 90°: 5 cm by 2 cm, 6 cm by 3.6 cm, 5 cm by 1 cm, and 4 cm by 4 cm. Which are rectangles and which are squares?
video_script.why: The child applies the angle rule for a rectangle and the extra side rule for a square, and sees that every square is also a rectangle.
video_script.substitution: Test the angles for the rectangle rule, then compare the sides of each shape for the square rule.
video_script.anchor: four quadrilaterals with square corners and sides 5 by 2, 6 by 3.6, 5 by 1 and 4 by 4 centimetres
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko says the four by four shape is a square, so it cannot be a rectangle; but it has four right angles, so it passes the rectangle test, and every square is also a rectangle.
video_script.payoff_line: All four are rectangles, and only the four by four one is also a square

final_answer.value: All four are rectangles; only the 4 cm by 4 cm one is also a square
final_answer.spoken: all four are rectangles, and only the four by four one is also a square

hold_back: only the 4 cm by 4 cm one is also a square
maths_rules: a rectangle is a quadrilateral in which all the angles are 90 degrees, so all four shapes are rectangles
a square is a quadrilateral in which all angles are 90 degrees and all sides are equal
5 by 2, 6 by 3.6 and 5 by 1 have unequal sides, so they are not squares
4 by 4 has equal sides, so it is also a square
every square is a rectangle, but not every rectangle is a square
video_script.design: One idea: rectangle by angles, square by angles and sides. Wrong idea: a square cannot be counted among the rectangles. The four shapes stay on the board throughout.
